title: Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence in the German Software Engineering Industry: An Empirical Study.
bounded_candidate_claim: Adoption depends on organizational, regulatory, experience, and interaction-depth conditions, so governance controls should not assume homogeneous tool use.

title: A Preliminary Study of Multilingual Code Language Models for Code Generation Task Using Translated Benchmarks.
bounded_candidate_claim: Translated code benchmarks can preserve some evaluation signals while still exhibiting cross-benchmark inconsistencies and reproducibility limits.

title: JavaBench: A Benchmark of Object-Oriented Code Generation for Evaluating Large Language Models.
bounded_candidate_claim: Function-level Python-heavy benchmark suites underrepresent object-oriented, class-level, project-level, and language-specific code generation.

title: An Agent-based Evaluation Framework for Complex Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Complex-code grading needs requirement-guided context and fine-grained criteria; reference-free model judging still requires validation for accuracy and explainability.

title: Code-DiTing: Automatic Evaluation of Code Generation without References or Test Cases.
bounded_candidate_claim: Reference-free code judging trades accuracy, explanation quality, prompt complexity, and inference cost rather than eliminating validation risk.

title: RealisticCodeBench: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Benchmarks mined from real developer use can test a different workload distribution than difficult repository tasks selected without evidence of actual tool use.

title: Robustness evaluation and enhancement of LLMs in code generation: an empirical study.
bounded_candidate_claim: Potential robustness evidence is in scope, but no abstract was available and no substantive claim should enter the manuscript before full-text verification.

title: PPM: Automated Generation of Diverse Programming Problems for Benchmarking Code Generation Models.
bounded_candidate_claim: Benchmark generation must test semantic diversity and contamination risk rather than scaling through homogeneous perturbations alone.

title: The Patch Overfitting Problem in Automated Program Repair: Practical Magnitude and a Baseline for Realistic Benchmarking.
bounded_candidate_claim: Patch-overfitting severity is workload- and tool-dependent; evaluation should compare assessment methods against a simple selection baseline instead of presuming a large plausible-patch set.

title: COFFE: A Code Efficiency Benchmark for Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Correctness-only code benchmarks miss execution efficiency, and timing protocols need stable, discriminating test cases before cost comparisons are credible.

title: CoderEval: A Benchmark of Pragmatic Code Generation with Generative Pre-trained Models.
bounded_candidate_claim: Standalone-function benchmarks omit the repository dependencies that dominate many real functions and therefore cannot establish pragmatic code-generation capability.

title: HumanEvo: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for More Realistic Evaluation of Repository-Level Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Repository-level evaluation should preserve the historical dependency state at the task point rather than supplying future project context.

title: Benchmarking Automated Program Repair: An Extensive Study on Both Real-World and Artificial Bugs.
bounded_candidate_claim: Using both real-world and artificial defect sets makes benchmark composition an explicit validity condition; any claim of differing repair behavior requires full-text verification.

title: Causality-Aided Evaluation and Explanation of Large Language Model-Based Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Evaluation can separate outcome scores from causal explanations of code-generation behavior, but the explanation method itself requires validation.

title: The First Prompt Counts the Most! An Evaluation of Large Language Models on Iterative Example-Based Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Iterative code-generation results can depend on first-prompt conditions, so correction-loop evaluations should control ordering and initial examples.

title: Seeing the Whole Elephant: Systematically Understanding and Uncovering Evaluation Biases in Automated Program Repair.
bounded_candidate_claim: Automated-repair evaluations contain recurring design biases that should be surfaced as a validity chain rather than collapsed into a success rate.

title: Poracle: Testing Patches under Preservation Conditions to Combat the Overfitting Problem of Program Repair.
bounded_candidate_claim: Patch oracles should test preservation conditions in addition to bug-triggering behavior to reduce plausible-but-regressive repairs.

title: Benchmarking and Categorizing the Performance of Neural Program Repair Systems for Java.
bounded_candidate_claim: Comparative repair evaluation benefits from a shared failure categorization instead of reporting aggregate repair counts alone.

title: HumanEvalComm: Benchmarking the Communication Competence of Code Generation for LLMs and LLM Agents.
bounded_candidate_claim: Coding-model evaluations should measure whether a system asks clarifying questions under ambiguous, incomplete, or inconsistent requirements separately from final code correctness.

title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Neural Program Repair with Natural Robustness Testing.
bounded_candidate_claim: Repair evaluation should test naturally occurring perturbations and robustness, not nominal benchmark accuracy alone.

title: MultiPL-E: A Scalable and Polyglot Approach to Benchmarking Neural Code Generation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Polyglot benchmark translation broadens language coverage but makes translation validity and per-language execution infrastructure part of the measurement contract.

title: LLM-Based Test-Driven Interactive Code Generation: User Study and Empirical Evaluation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Test-guided interaction can improve intent alignment, but evaluations must include the human effort and ambiguity-resolution cost of the loop.

title: Correlating Automated and Human Evaluation of Code Documentation Generation Quality.
bounded_candidate_claim: Automated documentation metrics require direct correlation against human judgments before they can serve as quality proxies.

title: The impact of human factors on the participation decision of reviewers in modern code review.
bounded_candidate_claim: Reviewer participation may depend on human and project-history factors, but the candidate claim requires version-of-record verification because exact-DOI enrichment supplied no abstract.

title: An Empirical Investigation of Relevant Changes and Automation Needs in Modern Code Review.
bounded_candidate_claim: Developers distinguish review tasks that need support from those suitable for automation; review tooling should preserve that task-level boundary.

title: Biases and differences in code review using medical imaging and eye-tracking: genders, humans, and machines.
bounded_candidate_claim: Human code review exhibits reviewer and apparent-author effects, so a human checkpoint is not automatically an unbiased ground truth.

title: Support, Not Automation: Towards AI-supported Code Review For Code Quality and Beyond.
bounded_candidate_claim: Code-review AI should be evaluated as support for quality and team outcomes rather than only as a path to full automation.

title: HalluJudge: A Reference-Free Hallucination Detection for Context Misalignment in Code Review Automation.
bounded_candidate_claim: Reference-free review-comment grounding checks have measurable effectiveness and cost boundaries and should remain calibrated against developer preferences.

title: An evidence-based inquiry into the use of grey literature in software engineering.
bounded_candidate_claim: Grey literature use in software-engineering research is increasing while empirical knowledge about its use remains limited; implications for quality and independence rules require full-text verification.

title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Use of Deep Learning in Software Engineering Research.
bounded_candidate_claim: The review organizes deep-learning-for-software-engineering evidence around learning components and surveyed successes, failures, and opportunities; any specific reporting-defect claim requires full-text verification.

title: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review.
bounded_candidate_claim: The LLM-for-software-engineering literature spans heterogeneous tasks, data, optimization, and evaluation practices, so the monograph should state its narrower reliability-system boundary.

title: Cognitive Biases in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study.
bounded_candidate_claim: Human verification remains exposed to documented cognitive biases, while evidence for effective mitigation in software engineering is limited.

title: Logging Practices in Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study.
bounded_candidate_claim: Logging research documents recurring implementation problems and low industry uptake of proposed solutions; observability protocols should therefore be tested operationally.

title: Machine/Deep Learning for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review.
bounded_candidate_claim: Reproducibility in ML-for-software-engineering depends on reporting data preparation, model selection, training, and evaluation details rather than model identity alone.
